blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe PPE removal for Airborne Precautions
stem: A nurse is leaving the room of a client on Airborne Precautions while wearing gloves, a gown, eye protection, and a fit-tested N95 respirator. Which removal plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Remove the gown, gloves, and eye protection before leaving, then remove the N95 just inside the doorway before exiting and closing the room door.
options.B: Leave the room wearing gown, gloves, eye protection, and N95; close the door, then remove and discard all PPE in the designated hallway area.
options.C: Remove PPE other than the N95 before leaving; clean hands after glove removal, exit and close the door, then remove the N95 and clean hands again.
options.D: Remove the gown and gloves in the room, but keep eye protection and the N95 on until reaching a clean staff area, then remove both together.

rationale: C is correct. Current CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices direct healthcare personnel to remove and discard PPE other than respirators before leaving the patient's room or care area. When a respirator is used, CDC states that it should be removed after leaving the room or care area and closing the door. CDC hand-hygiene guidance in the same core-practices document requires hand hygiene immediately after glove removal. The item therefore avoids prescribing a universal order among gown, gloves, and eye protection while preserving the critical room-boundary and respirator rules. A is incorrect because it removes the N95 before the nurse has exited and closed the door. B is incorrect because gown, gloves, and eye protection should not be carried into the hallway for routine doffing. D is incorrect because eye protection is PPE other than the respirator and should be removed before leaving the patient room or care area rather than worn onward to a clean staff area.
educational_objective: Safely doff PPE for Airborne Precautions by removing non-respirator PPE before leaving the room, performing indicated hand hygiene, and removing the N95 only after exiting and closing the door.
source_organization: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC Core Practices page dated 2024-04-12 and current when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Core Practices lines 113-120: select/use appropriate PPE; remove and discard PPE other than respirators before leaving the patient's room or care area; if a respirator is used, remove it after leaving the room/care area and closing the door; train HCP to remove/dispose of PPE in a way that protects themselves, patients, and others. CDC hand-hygiene lines 79-86 require hand hygiene at specified indications including immediately after glove removal. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed page 8 / PDF screenshot pageno 11: protect clients and healthcare personnel from health/environmental hazards, apply infection-prevention principles including isolation/standard enhanced barrier precautions, and use PPE appropriately.
source_claim_supported: Fresh current CDC HTML directly supports removal of non-respirator PPE before room exit, respirator removal only after exiting and closing the door, and immediate hand hygiene after glove removal. The final item intentionally does not assert a universal sequence among gown, gloves, and eye protection. NCSBN supports the infection-prevention/PPE blueprint construct.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed page 8 / PDF screenshot pageno 11: protect clients and healthcare personnel from hazards; apply infection-prevention/isolation principles; use PPE and safety measures appropriately.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — the official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was freshly screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation on 2026-08-20. CDC evidence used for Q0064 is current HTML; no CDC PDF evidence is relied on.
correction_summary: Original Q0064 contained an absolute-word distractor and mixed obviously unsafe workflows with the correct sequence. The item was rebuilt so each alternative reflects a plausible doffing-location or timing error. The final key tests the CDC-supported distinction between non-respirator PPE removal before room exit and respirator removal after exit/door closure, without imposing a brittle universal ordering among gown, gloves, and eye protection.

option_audit.A: Plausible near-correct sequence; incorrect only at the critical airborne step because the N95 is removed before exiting and closing the door.
option_audit.B: Plausible hallway-doffing shortcut; incorrect because non-respirator PPE should be removed before leaving the patient room/care area.
option_audit.C: Correct; preserves non-respirator PPE removal before exit, hand hygiene after glove removal, and N95 removal after exit and door closure.
option_audit.D: Plausible clean-zone shortcut; incorrect because eye protection is non-respirator PPE and should not be carried to a clean staff area for later removal.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 145, B 141, C 146, D 140 characters; the correct answer is not conspicuously longer and choices are tightly balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options describe realistic PPE-removal workflows and differ primarily in where/when non-respirator PPE and the N95 are removed.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. A removes the N95 too early, B carries contaminated non-respirator PPE outside the room, and D carries eye protection to a clean area. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
